claims.claim: The Introduction to the micro:bit lessons use a Think, Create, Evaluate, Extend, Share sequence, with the Create phase supporting code examination, building, tutorials, and coding-video scaffolds.
For young children, retain the lesson cycle but keep each session centered on one observable input-to-output idea, such as pressing a button to change LEDs or shaking the device to trigger an action.
Use the Think phase to elicit a short prediction about a familiar physical action before introducing the matching code, which makes the micro:bit behavior concrete and reduces novice cognitive load.
Present one new concept or action per slide, supported by a large visual of the micro:bit and a brief teacher-led demonstration, before asking children to reproduce it in Create.
Make Evaluate a brief show-and-tell or teacher observation against a visible success criterion, because the current course provenance identifies missing formal assessment in several sessions.
Offer Extend as an optional, clearly bounded choice after the core build works, so younger learners can finish the essential task at a comfortable pace while early finishers remain engaged.

End Share with a pair demonstration and a simple sentence stem describing what the program does, reinforcing the course's existing objective-review and sharing pattern without adding a heavy written task.
